title: The geometric case of the Erdős similarity conjecture
assumptions: The ratio q is fixed and lies strictly between 0 and 1.
The pattern being avoided is the geometric progression {q^n : n ≥ 1}, up to translation and nontrivial dilation.
The constructed set may depend on q; the result does not claim one set works for several ratios at once.
conclusion: For every fixed q in (0,1) and every η in (0,1), the paper constructs a compact subset of [0,1] of measure greater than 1−η that contains no nontrivial affine copy of {q^n : n ≥ 1}. In the one case covered by the upstream Lean scope (q = 1/2), the same avoidance is stated for every translation and every nonzero real dilation.
notProven: The upstream Lean scope covers only the dyadic sequence {2^-n : n ≥ 1}. The general ratio q in (0,1) is not covered by the linked Lean statement.
The paper does not assert one set that simultaneously avoids copies for different ratios; its set may depend on q.
No Proofweave replay is recorded for either manuscript (proofweaveReplay: not_run), and no statement review is recorded (statementReview: not_started).
The snapshot does not show whether the general-q argument has been formalized elsewhere upstream; that remains unknown (needs review).
The construction makes the measure arbitrarily close to one, not equal to one: the complement may have positive measure.
scopeNote: The paper's stated result covers every fixed geometric ratio q in (0,1). The Lean scope document included in the pinned snapshot proves the dyadic case q = 1/2 only. This draft presents that gap as a scope difference; it does not claim that the general case has been platform-verified.

scopeDiff.paperStatement: For every fixed $`q\in(0,1)`$, constructs compact subsets of $`[0,1]`$ with measure arbitrarily close to one containing no translated and nontrivially dilated copy of $`\{q^n:n\ge1\}`$, with dilations of either sign. This resolves the geometric-progression case of the Erdős similarity conjecture for every ratio.
scopeDiff.leanStatement: The formalization proves the dyadic case of the Erdős similarity conjecture. For every $0<\eta<1$, it constructs a compact set $E\subset[0,1]$ of measure greater than $1-\eta$ that contains no affine copy of $\{2^{-n}:n\ge1\}$. Explicitly, for every translation $x$ and every nonzero real dilation $s$, some point $x+s2^{-n}$ lies outside $E$. Both signs of $s$ are included.
scopeDiff.gapNote: Paper: every fixed ratio q in (0,1). Lean scope: the dyadic ratio {2^-n} only, with both signs of dilation.
scopeDiff.platformStatus: Not run: both manuscripts report proofweaveReplay not_run, statementReview not_started, and no receipt.

proofSteps.label: Construct a compact set with measure greater than 1−η

glossary.definition: A sequence of the form {q^n : n ≥ 1} for a fixed ratio q.
A set of the form x + sA = {x + s·a : a ∈ A} for a translation x and a dilation s.
Refers to powers of two, here the sequence {2^-n : n ≥ 1}.
Lebesgue measure on the interval [0,1]. Measure greater than 1−η means the complement is small but may be nonempty.
